newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end mixed, views differ.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end mixed, views differ.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed in active trading on Tuesday with investors holding different opinions about the short-term trend, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 20,350 yuan ($2,453) per tonne, unchanged from Monday's close.
It opened at an intraday high of 20,500 and hit a low of 20,260 yuan per tonne.

July fell 120 to 20,280, August was unchanged at 20,300, September was unchanged at 20,300, October rose 30 to 20,380, December fell 10 to 20,350 and the January 1998 contract dropped 80 to 20,320 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 78,970 tonnes from 50,630 tonnes.
Copper opened higher but proit-taking pushed prices down for most of the session.
Traders said overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME) had boosted the confidence of long-position holders in Shanghai but the general outlook was still not clear.
"Some investors continued to liquidate their long positions at high levels today due to a lack of clear positive market-moving news," one trader said.
"Active trading indicated many investors hold mixed opinions about the short-term market trend," he added.
Three months copper was looking to fill a gap up to $2,365 on Tuesday, after firming near the day's highs on Monday at $2,315, analysts in London said.
Physical prices in Shanghai were around 20,350 yuan per tonne on Tuesday as end-users continued to avoid buying.
Traders said the weak buying interest could lead to sharp falls in the short term.
"Copper is likely to move around the 20,000-yuan level in the next few days, waiting for new developments," a second trader said.
Aluminium futures ended down across the board.
July fell 70 to 13,420, August 20 to 13,530, September 50 to 13,740, October 60 to 13,680, November 50 to 13,650 and December 50 to 13,650 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 3,660 tonnes from 3,630 tonnes.
